name: Hashed email and phone identity graphs (UID2, RampID)
plain: Ad firms turn a hashed email or phone into a shared ID that follows people across apps and sites.
meaning: When device IDs are blocked, a login or email is the best key. Graphs link logins to ads across publishers, and they rely on the person having signed in.

android.store_policy: Data safety: sharing; User Data policy
android.api_surface: UID2 SDK, LiveRamp ATS, ID5, server-side APIs
android.note: Matching uses normalized, hashed email or phone.

ios.store_policy: Counts as tracking under ATT if sent to third parties for ads
ios.note: Sign in with Apple private relay emails defeat matching.

data.metric: SHA-256 email or phone to UID2 or RampID token

limits.headline: Can match you across apps and sites using your email or phone, scrambled into an ID
limits.user_action: You sign in or give your email or phone to an app or site
can: Turn your email or phone into a scrambled code and share that code with ad partners
Recognize you in other apps and websites that use the same system
Work on both Android and iPhone through ad SDKs and server to server links
cannot: Match you if you never give an email or phone to any partner
Match you when you use Hide My Email; Apple's relay address breaks the link
Use your real email directly; partners share the scrambled version
Work after you opt out where the ID provider offers an opt out
limits.reach_label: Follows you across apps and sites
limits.differs: Hide My Email on iPhone can break matching. Android sign in gives apps your real email.

story.what_it_is: Ad companies turn your email or phone into a shared scrambled ID that follows you across apps and sites.

marketing.name: UID2
marketing.pitch: Pitch: an open ID built from an email or phone that lets advertisers reach people on the open internet with privacy controls.

story.for_you: You type your email to read an article or sign in to a shopping app. Later, ads on other apps and sites may seem to know you. You never see the scrambled ID that links them.
story.for_makers: With device IDs fading, a login is the best key for ads. Publishers sell logged in audiences, and advertisers match their customer lists to them. It only works when people sign in.

use_cases.example: A news site asks you to sign in with an email, then sells ad space to brands that can recognize you by a scrambled copy of it.
A retailer uploads its customer list to an ad network so you see its ads on other apps.
A streaming service lets advertisers reach logged in viewers across phone and TV.
A brand measures whether a TV ad made a known customer buy later in an app.
A game with a login shares a hashed email with an ad partner to find look alike players.
Fraud teams check if one hashed email is tied to hundreds of fake sign ups.

risks: Follows you across apps and sites
story.android_note: Works the same way on Android, with the ad ID as one more signal.
story.ios_note: Works on iPhone too. Sign in with Apple's hidden email stops it.

technical_bounds: Apple relay emails cannot be matched

abuse: Linking users across apps without disclosure

history.change: ATT pushes advertisers to log-in-based IDs
Mobile SDKs released for Android and iOS
